tutorial.title: Forms with Labels
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn how to add labels to your form in HTML

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent:
In games, HUD labels are important for showing the player what a value means. Fill in label inside of the blank space.

Make sure to type label.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
We create a label by using the <label> and </label> tags.

Make sure to pick <label>, followed by </label>.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
We add text to labels to help players know what a HUD value represents. Add Score as the text after the second label tag.

Make sure to pick Score.

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
The for attribute specifies which element a label is bound to. Its value is the same as the id value of the linked element.

Make sure to type for.

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
The for attribute value must be the same as the value of the id of the corresponding element. Add "mana" as a value for the for attribute.

Make sure to pick mana.

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
Labels also help with accessibility. Screen readers will audibly read labels like Health: or Score: when the linked element is in focus.

Additionally, when a player clicks on the label, the connected element will be focused on.

Make sure to pick Health, followed by Score.

lessons.title: Lesson #7
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can use placeholder attributes within input fields to act like labels. However, this is not a complete replacement for labels.

Make sure to pick placeholder.

lessons.title: Lesson #8
lessons.interactiveContent:
Why do we use labels in interfaces?

We use labels to explain what a value or control in the UI representsWe use labels as an alternative to canvas in HTML

We use labels to explain what a value or control in the UI represents.

lessons.title: Lesson #9
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's wrong with the code?

It should use label elements instead of p elementsThere shouldn't be any line break elements

It should use label elements instead of p elements.

lessons.title: Lesson #10
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does the label for the score value say?

Score:Level:

Make sure to pick Score:.

lessons.title: Lesson #11
lessons.interactiveContent:
Why do we use the for attribute in a label element?

To link between the UI element and the label elementTo describe the type of label element

To link between the UI element and the label element.

lessons.title: Lesson #12
lessons.interactiveContent:
What should the for attribute of the Volume label be in order to connect it to the input with id="volume"?

volumedifficulty

Make sure to pick volume.

lessons.title: Lesson #13
lessons.interactiveContent:
How do labels help with accessibility?

Screen readers will read the label when the linked element is focused onLabels only provide decorative text

Screen readers will read the label when the linked element is focused on.

lessons.title: Lesson #14
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does this code display?

A form with a textbox input with the text Level Code insideA form with a label with the text Level Code next to an input

A form with a textbox input with the text Level Code inside.

lessons.title: Lesson #15
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code the label element's opening tag.

Make sure to type <label>.

lessons.title: Lesson #16
lessons.interactiveContent:
Create a label with the text Difficulty:.

Make sure to pick <label>, followed by Difficulty:, and finally </label>.

lessons.title: Lesson #17
lessons.interactiveContent:
Fill in the for attribute in the label to match the id of the enemy count input field.

Make sure to type enemyCount.

lessons.title: Lesson #18
lessons.interactiveContent:
Add a for attribute in the label attribute to match the id of the input for player.

Make sure to type for="player".

lessons.title: Lesson #19
lessons.interactiveContent:
Add the correct label element with the text Character:.

Make sure to pick <label for="character">, followed by Character:, and finally </label>.

lessons.title: Lesson #20
lessons.interactiveContent:
Set a placeholder for the input as an alternative to using a label.

Make sure to pick placeholder, followed by =, and finally "Enter Code".
